ITEM.PTXT: The front drive shafts of vehicles with the 2GR-FE engine use Rzeppa type constant velocity joints on the axle side and tripod type constant velocity joints on the transaxle side on both the left and right.
A GF1A type transfer has been adopted on 4WD models.

It is located on the right side of the drive shaft output section of the transaxle. It changes the direction of the driving force input to the differential case by 90 degrees and outputs it to the rear. The driven pinion gear is mounted with an upward offset relative to the ring gear.
The driven pinion gear is hollow, and a unit ball bearing is used to support it, resulting in a compact, lightweight construction.
A left/right split aluminum die-cast transfer case has been adopted, making the case compact and lightweight.
A spline connection is used to secure the ring gear and ring gear mount, providing a compact, lightweight connection.
A side lip contact type oil seal has been adopted for excellent resistance to muddy water.
A 2-shaft, 3-joint type using shell type and tripod type constant velocity joints has been adopted.
Quietness is ensured by optimizing the center support position, adopting compact, lightweight tripod type constant velocity joints and improving balance accuracy.

Active Torque Control 4WD has been adopted. By controlling the transmitted torque of the electronically controlled coupling located at the front of the rear differential, the front/rear torque distribution is continuously varied between the front-wheel drive state and direct-coupled 4WD, achieving optimum driving force distribution under various driving conditions for stability and low fuel consumption.
A differential limiting mechanism, as in a typical full-time 4WD, is not required, and the system has been simplified to reduce size and weight.

ENTRY.PTXT: Stable starting and acceleration on slippery roads such as snowy roads, equivalent to direct-coupled 4WD
Low fuel consumption by distributing torque to the rear wheels only when needed and only as much as needed

ITEM.PTXT: The torque transmitted to the rear wheels is controlled by the Active Torque Control 4WD computer to achieve the optimum front/rear torque distribution based on input signals from various sensors.

ITEM.PTXT: Turning the 4WD auto mode switch ON switches to 4WD auto mode, and control is performed to achieve both "traction performance" and "avoidance of the tight corner braking phenomenon".

During normal driving, the engine driving torque is calculated from signals such as throttle opening, engine speed and shift position, and the torque transmitted to the rear wheels is optimally controlled to ensure maximum acceleration performance.

When it is determined from the throttle opening signal and wheel speed signals that the driver's operation and the vehicle are stable, the torque transmitted to the rear wheels is lowered to a state close to front-wheel drive, contributing to improved fuel economy.

ENTRY.PTXT: By optimally distributing the total driving torque estimated from the engine torque to the front and rear wheels, starting performance equivalent to direct-coupled 4WD is ensured. Also, torque transmission to the rear wheels is optimized to avoid the tight corner braking phenomenon that occurs during low-speed turns.

ITEM.PTXT: The tight corner braking phenomenon is a condition in which, when a rotation difference between the front and rear wheels is required, such as during turning, a 4WD vehicle with directly coupled front and rear wheels cannot absorb this rotation difference when driving in 4-wheel drive, resulting in a state as if the brakes were applied.

ENTRY.PTXT: During braking deceleration, 4WD auto mode is canceled to increase the effectiveness of ABS and VSC control.

ITEM.PTXT: When the 4WD auto mode switch is turned OFF, 4WD control is stopped and torque transmission to the rear wheels is cut, resulting in an FF (front-wheel drive) state. This enables driving aimed at improving fuel economy.

If there is a malfunction in the 4WD system, the master warning indicator light illuminates, "4WD Check" is displayed on the multi-information display, and 4WD control is stopped and the vehicle switches to front-wheel drive.

If excessive driving may damage the drive system, the 4WD auto mode indicator blinks, and 4WD control is stopped and the vehicle switches to front-wheel drive. By cooling the drive system without turning off the engine, 4WD control becomes possible again.
The electronically controlled coupling consists of a main clutch, control clutch, front housing, shaft, armature, cam, piston and electromagnetic solenoid.

2 types of clutches are provided: the control clutch and the main clutch. The aim is to amplify the torque generated by the control clutch with the cam and generate even greater torque with the main clutch, producing sufficient torque while keeping the actuator (electromagnetic solenoid + control clutch + armature) compact and achieving a high level of torque generation response.

The control clutch is a metal multi-plate clutch so that it can pass magnetic flux, and because the main clutch generates several times the torque of the control clutch and does a large amount of work, a wet multi-plate clutch has been adopted for it. The surface treatment and groove shape of the metal clutch have been refined to ensure high durability and driving force transmission efficiency.
For both the main clutch and control clutch, the outer side is engaged with the front housing and the inner side with the shaft (the control clutch is engaged with the cam).

Driving force from the transfer is transmitted from the propeller shaft to the front housing. When the electromagnetic solenoid is not operating, the main clutch and control clutch are each free, so driving force is not transmitted from the front housing to the shaft, and driving force from the transfer is not transmitted to the rear wheels.

When current flows through the electromagnetic solenoid, magnetic flux is generated around the electromagnetic solenoid. (A non-magnetic section is provided in the rear housing so that the magnetic flux does not converge only at the electromagnetic solenoid.) The attraction force of this electromagnet pulls the armature toward the control clutch, engaging the control clutch.

When the control clutch is engaged while there is a rotation difference between the front and rear wheels, the balls push on the slope of the cam engaged with the shaft, and the cam rotates. The rotation of the cam causes the piston to press against the main clutch, engaging the main clutch.
Driving force from the front housing is transmitted through the main clutch to the shaft and then to the rear differential, transmitting driving force to the rear wheels.

When there is a rotation difference between the front and rear wheels, the amount of driving force transmitted to the rear wheels is steplessly controlled by controlling the current flowing through the electromagnetic solenoid.

When the current is small, the force with which the armature restrains the control clutch is small, so the force with which the cam presses the piston is weak and the pressure applied to the main clutch is low. As a result, the driving force transmitted by the main clutch is small, and the driving force from the propeller shaft is transmitted to the rear wheels in a limited amount.

When the current increases, the force with which the armature restrains the control clutch becomes stronger, the force with which the cam presses the piston also becomes stronger, and the pressure applied to the main clutch increases. As a result, the driving force transmitted by the main clutch increases, and power is transmitted in a state close to direct-coupled 4WD.

ITEM.PTXT: A 2-pinion type front differential with helical gears for the reduction mechanism and straight bevel gears for the differential mechanism has been adopted.
A compact, lightweight FD13B type differential with an integrated electronically controlled coupling has been adopted.
A left/right split type aluminum die-cast carrier case has been adopted, achieving a significant weight reduction.
Vibration-isolating support at 2 front points and 1 rear points using rubber cushions via the differential support reduces vibration and noise.
An aluminum mount bracket has been adopted to reduce weight.
225/45R17 90W size tires & 17× 7J size aluminum wheels have been adopted on 2GR-FE engine models.
Center ornaments have been provided on the aluminum wheels.
A T125/70D17 98M size spare tire is provided on all models.
